providers.name: OpenRouter (free models)
providers.summary: Many open models for free with one key. Good for trying the agent and for small sites.
providers.limits: Free models allow about 20 messages a minute and 50 a day, or 1,000 a day once you have bought $10 of credits.
providers.privacy: Some free models are run by providers that may keep or learn from what is sent. Name the AI provider in your privacy policy.
steps: Create a free account at openrouter.ai.
Open Keys and press Create key. Name it after your site.
Copy the key (it starts with sk-or-), paste it into the API key box below and save.
Press Test connection. If a free model is busy, pick another one from the list.

providers.name: Groq (free plan)
providers.summary: Very fast replies, which suits a voice agent. The free plan needs no card.
providers.limits: The free plan allows about 30 messages a minute and 1,000 a day for each model.
providers.privacy: Groq runs the models on its own servers. Name it as your AI provider in your privacy policy.
steps: Sign up at console.groq.com (a Google or GitHub account works).
Open API Keys and press Create API Key.
Copy the key (it starts with gsk_), paste it into the API key box below and save.
Press Test connection.

providers.name: Google Gemini (free tier)
providers.summary: Google's fast models. The free tier needs only a Google account.
providers.limits: The free tier has a daily limit for each model. Turn on billing in Google AI Studio to raise it.
providers.privacy: On the free tier Google may use what is sent to improve its products. With billing turned on, it does not.
steps: Go to aistudio.google.com and sign in with a Google account.
Press Get API key, then Create API key.
Copy the key, paste it into the API key box below and save.
Press Test connection.

providers.name: DeepSeek
providers.summary: Strong answers at a very low price. Pay as you go.
providers.limits: Pay as you go: a small balance, such as $2, lasts a long time for a chat agent.
providers.privacy: DeepSeek processes requests on its own servers. Name it as your AI provider in your privacy policy.
steps: Create an account at platform.deepseek.com.
Add a balance under Top up. A few dollars is enough to start.
Open API Keys, press Create new API key and copy it (it starts with sk-).
Paste it into the API key box below, save and press Test connection.

providers.name: OpenAI (GPT)
providers.summary: OpenAI's GPT models. Pay as you go.
providers.limits: Pay as you go. Add credit under Billing before the key works.
providers.privacy: OpenAI does not train on API data by default. Name it as your AI provider in your privacy policy.
steps: Sign in at platform.openai.com.
Add credit under Settings, Billing.
Open API keys, press Create new secret key and copy it (it starts with sk-).
Paste it into the API key box below, save and press Test connection.

providers.name: Anthropic (Claude)
providers.summary: Claude models from Anthropic: careful, natural conversation. Pay as you go.
providers.limits: Pay as you go. Add credit under Billing before the key works.
providers.privacy: Anthropic does not train on API data by default. Name it as your AI provider in your privacy policy.
steps: Sign in at platform.claude.com.
Add credit under Billing.
Open API keys, press Create key and copy it (it starts with sk-ant-).
Paste it into the API key box below, save and press Test connection.

n8n.name: Northflank + Supabase (free)
n8n.cost: Free. Northflank asks for a card to verify the account, but the free plan charges nothing if you add no paid extras.
steps: Supabase: sign up at supabase.com (GitHub sign-in works) and press New project. Pick a region near you, press Generate a password and save it somewhere safe. Switch the Data API off, n8n does not need it.
In the new project press Connect, choose Session pooler and note the host (aws-0-your-region.pooler.supabase.com), the port 5432, the database postgres and the user (postgres.your-project-ref).

Northflank: sign up at northflank.com, create a project, then add a Service and choose Deploy a Docker image. Use the image docker.io/n8nio/n8n:latest and the free plan (nf-compute-20). Add port 5678 as public HTTP.

Add these environment variables: DB_TYPE=postgresdb, DB_POSTGRESDB_HOST, DB_POSTGRESDB_PORT=5432, DB_POSTGRESDB_DATABASE=postgres, DB_POSTGRESDB_USER, DB_POSTGRESDB_PASSWORD, DB_POSTGRESDB_SSL_ENABLED=true, DB_POSTGRESDB_SSL_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=false, N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY (a long random text you keep a copy of), N8N_PROTOCOL=https, N8N_PORT=5678, N8N_PROXY_HOPS=1, NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=384, EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE=true, EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE=168 and GENERIC_TIMEZONE.

After the first deploy, copy the service's public address and add N8N_HOST (the address without https://), plus N8N_EDITOR_BASE_URL and N8N_WEBHOOK_URL (the full address ending in /). Save and restart.
The first start takes about five minutes on the free plan. Then open the address and create your n8n owner account.
Download the workflow on this page, and in n8n choose Workflows, Import from file.

Open the Webhook node and create a Header Auth credential: Name X-Voice-Agent-Secret, Value = the webhook secret shown on this page. Add your Telegram and email credentials to the alert nodes, or delete the nodes you do not need.
Press Publish. Copy the webhook's Production URL into Webhook URL on the Alerts tab, switch the webhook on and press Send test.
notes: Do not add a volume on Northflank: volumes are billed, and n8n keeps everything in Supabase.
The free plan has 512 MB of memory. That is plenty for lead alerts, but not for heavy AI workflows inside n8n.
Keep N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY safe. Without it n8n cannot read the credentials it saved.

n8n.name: n8n Cloud
n8n.cost: Paid monthly plan with a free trial. Nothing to install or maintain.
steps: Start a trial at n8n.io and open your workspace.
Download the workflow on this page, then choose Workflows, Import from file.
Create the Header Auth credential (Name X-Voice-Agent-Secret, Value = the webhook secret on this page) and your Telegram and email credentials.
Press Publish, copy the webhook's Production URL into Webhook URL on the Alerts tab and press Send test.

n8n.name: Any VPS with Docker
n8n.cost: From about $5 a month for a small server.
steps: Rent a small Linux server and install Docker.
Run n8n with the official image docker.io/n8nio/n8n behind HTTPS (for example with Caddy or Traefik), following n8n's self-hosting guide.
Import the workflow from this page and set up the credentials as in the steps above.
Publish it, then paste the webhook's Production URL into Webhook URL on the Alerts tab and press Send test.
